reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every natural number n >= 3 and every real number κ >= 4, set
s = sqrt(κ),
r = (1 - 1/n)(s - 1)/(s + 1), and
ℓ = (4ns + (s - 1)^2)/(8n(n - 1)).
Let μ be normalized Haar probability measure on the entire real orthogonal group O(n), including both determinant signs. For O in O(n), write U(O) = O_{00} and define
q(O) = ((s + 1)U(O) - (s - 1)) / (1 + r^2 - 2rU(O))^(n/2).
Let γ_O be the centered Gaussian measure on Euclidean R^n with covariance
C_O = [((κ + 1)/2)I_n - ((κ - 1)/4)(O + O^T)]^(-1).
Then q is absolutely integrable with respect to μ, and
∫_{O(n)} det(O) [∫_{R^n} exp(-ℓ ||x||_2^2) dγ_O(x)] dμ(O)
= [(-1)^(n-1)(s - 1)^(n-1)/(s + 1)^n] (1 - 1/n)^(n/2) ∫_{O(n)} q(O) dμ(O).
Here n/2 in real powers is a real exponent, all dimensional fractions use real arithmetic, and n-1 in the integer powers is the natural-number difference.

For each O, γ_O is the centered multivariate Gaussian built from covariance C_O, the nonsingular inverse of ((κ+1)/2)I - ((κ-1)/4)(O+O^T).
